dedupe_keys.name: large scale clogging experiments assessing the hydraulic performance of porous asphalt during their service life

description: Angélica Vanessa Goya Heredia and colleagues at Universidade da Coruña report eleven clogging experiments on porous asphalt retrofitting a 36 m² laboratory street section. Sediment loads accumulate to 5.5 kg/m² between thirty-minute rainfall events of 80 mm/h. Measurements include permeability, internal water levels, flow, turbidity and suspended solids. The source reports surface clogging from 4 kg/m² and 93% sediment retention, while noting that small specimens omit heterogeneity affecting full-scale fluxes. The source identifies the measurements as inputs for permeable-pavement simulations. Coverage is a controlled physical infrastructure testbed; the experiments do not represent a measured service lifetime in an operating street. Zenodo provides the article freely under CC BY 4.0. The abstract states that an experimental dataset exists, but this deposit lists only the article and no separate dataset link. A limitation is that data values, article bodies and transferability were not independently checked. Related pavement experiments use different materials or scales.
